research_rationale: EO 11623 (signed October 12, 1971; 36 FR 19963) delegates to the Director of Selective Service the authority to issue rules and regulations under the Military Selective Service Act (section 1) and sets the consultation, referral and publication procedure for those rules (section 2(a) to (c)), with a rule of construction preserving the President's own authority (section 3). I read the complete held Federal Register original; its five dossier clauses match the order's own structure (sections 1, 2(a), 2(b), 2(c) and 3), so the inventory is confirmed without correction. The order has no sunset or ending condition. Two held later orders amend it: EO 12608 section 15 (September 9, 1987; Health and Human Services for Health, Education, and Welfare) and EO 13286 section 60 (effective March 1, 2003; Homeland Security for Transportation in section 2(a)); both are attached as later events on section 2(a) with before and after wording, and the U.S. Code note printing the order lists exactly these two amendments. The dossier also lists EO 12977 as a later event; the text it offers is EO 13286's section 60 under an EO 12977 queue label, and the held text of EO 12977 (60 FR 54411) does not name EO 11623, so EO 12977 is not a later event. The held regulations and notices that cite the order (FR Doc. 94-31721, 95-6288, 04-2427 and 04-8606, and 32 CFR parts 1602, 1605 and 1609 authority lines) apply it and do not end it. The three bounded searches record no revocation or supersession. All five clauses are operative on the original text as amended, checked through 2026-10-14.
savings_reason: EO 11623 has no savings or transition clause other than the continuation of earlier presidential regulations in section 1, which is not an accrued right of an ended clause; no held order revokes or replaces it, so no residual effect arises.
earlier_end_check: Own text: no end date or condition in sections 1 to 3 (the until wording in section 1 limits how long earlier presidential regulations continue, not the delegation; the 10 and 30 day periods in section 2 are procedural waiting periods; the later date in section 2(c) fixes when a rule takes effect). A search of the held texts for the number 11623 finds EO 12608, EO 13286, regulations and notices that apply the order, and OFR and U.S. Code notes; none revokes or supersedes it.
scope_check: Five clauses follow the order: section 1 (delegation and continuation of earlier regulations), section 2(a) (consultation), 2(b) (referral and 30-day wait), 2(c) (publication and effective date), section 3 (rule of construction). Only section 2(a) is amended (EO 12608 section 15, EO 13286 section 60).
independent_command_check: The delegation, the three procedural duties and the rule of construction are standing rules that apply each time the Director issues a rule; none is a report, deadline or one-time task. The continuation of earlier presidential regulations in section 1 is a transitional command whose completion is not shown, and the claim does not rely on it.
savings_check: No savings, transition or accrued-rights clause ended; nothing held revokes or replaces the order, so no residual effect arises.

research_rationale: EO 11935 (41 FR 37301, signed September 2, 1976) amends Civil Service Rule VII (5 CFR Part 7) by adding a new section 7.4, Citizenship: only citizens or nationals of the United States may be admitted to competitive examination or appointed in the competitive service, with an exception the Commission may authorize by law for aliens in specific cases or temporary appointments. I read the complete held Federal Register original; the order is one paragraph with one added section and no sunset or condition, so the dossier's single clause is the complete inventory. Held later instruments: EO 12107 (signed December 28, 1978; effective January 1, 1979 under its section 2-404) substitutes the Office of Personnel Management for the Civil Service Commission in the orders listed in its section 2-101, which includes EO 11935; it is attached as a later event. EO 13940 (2020) recites EO 11935 in a compliance-review direction and does not amend it. A June 30, 2026 OPM final rule (FR Doc. 2026-13154) restates the rule as existing law. The held 5 CFR 7.3 source note records the redesignation by EO 13197 (January 25, 2001); the held text of EO 13197 renumbers section 7.4 as 7.3 and lists 7.3 Citizenship in its table of sections, so it keeps the rule. That text is held in the repository but is not a packet evidence record, so the claim describes it and does not cite it as a later event. A search of the held texts for the number 11935 finds only EO 12107's list, EO 13940, Federal Register pages that cite or apply the order, and CFR texts that apply it; none revokes or supersedes it. The bounded searches (U.S. Code, eCFR, Federal Register catalog dispositions) record no revocation or supersession. The clause continues on the original text as amended, checked through 2026-10-14.
savings_reason: The order has no savings clause and its single clause has not ended, so no residual from an ended clause arises.
earlier_end_check: No own-terms end. A search of the held texts for the number 11935 finds EO 12107 (which lists it), EO 13940 (a recital), Federal Register pages that cite or apply it, and CFR texts that apply it; none revokes or supersedes it. EO 12107 changes the agency named; EO 13197 renumbers the section; neither ends the rule.
scope_check: The order is one paragraph adding one section (7.4) of three paragraphs to the Civil Service Rules, treated as one clause (EO:11935#whole) covering the whole order in the held 41 FR 37301 original.
independent_command_check: Paragraphs (a), (b) and (c) of the added section are parts of one rule: the two citizenship bars and the exception. None is a report, deadline or completable task; held 5 CFR 7.3 and the 2026 OPM rule show the rule continuing.
savings_check: No savings clause in the order, and no ended clause leaves a residual.

research_rationale: EO 13736 (signed August 12, 2016; 81 FR 54711, Federal Register issue of August 17, 2016) provides an order of succession within the Department of Veterans Affairs under the Federal Vacancies Reform Act of 1998. I read the complete held Federal Register text: an authority paragraph; section 1 (ten listed officials, (a) to (j), who act as Secretary when both the Secretary and the Deputy Secretary are unable to serve); section 2 (exceptions (a) to (c)); section 3 (four revocations: EO 13247, section 4(g) of EO 13261, and two presidential memoranda of March 19, 2002 and February 12, 2003); section 4 (no rights created). I corrected the machine inventory: entries (d) and (e) of the section 1 list are one clause, the two OCR fragments of section 2(b) are one clause, and the span of section 3(d) stops before the page footer. Section 3's four revocations are self-executing and were performed on August 12, 2016, the only effective date the text states or implies, so those four clauses are terminated by performance; the revoked instruments stay revoked, which is a consequence and not a command of this order. All other clauses have no end date or ending condition. A search of the held texts for the number 13736 finds the order only in its own Federal Register copies, the Federal Register notice of the order, an OFR table that lists it with no disposition note, and a 5 U.S.C. 3345 note that cites it; no held later order, statute or regulation amends, revokes or supersedes it. The three selected searches (U.S. Code through 2026-10-09, eCFR as of 2026-10-14, Federal Register executive-order catalog disposition notes) record no revocation or supersession. The operative clauses therefore continue on the original text, checked through 2026-10-14.
savings_reason: EO 13736 has no savings, transition or accrued-rights clause, and no held later order revokes or replaces it, so no residual effect arises. The section 3 revocations are exhausted by performance; the order of succession is a continuing standing rule, not an accrued right.
earlier_end_check: Own text: sections 1, 2 and 4 have no end date, duration or condition. Section 3 revokes four earlier instruments and is performed on issuance. The held-text number search finds no later revocation, supersession or amendment of EO 13736, and the catalog search has no disposition note, so nothing ends the continuing clauses before 2026-10-14.
scope_check: Section 1 lists the succession order, with entries (a) to (j) (entries (d) and (e) share one clause); section 2 limits the list and preserves presidential discretion; section 4 disclaims enforceable rights. Section 3(a) to (d) are four separate one-time revocations, each terminated by performance on August 12, 2016. No operative clause is partial or time-limited.
independent_command_check: The succession list and exceptions are standing rules that apply whenever a vacancy occurs; they are not reports, deadlines or completable tasks. The four revocations are exhausted one-time commands and are recorded as terminated; they do not affect the continuing clauses.
savings_check: The order has no savings, transition or accrued-rights clause. Nothing held revokes or replaces EO 13736, and the revocations in section 3 are of other instruments, so no residual effect arises.

research_rationale: EO 12905 (signed March 25, 1994; 59 FR 14733) establishes the Trade and Environment Policy Advisory Committee in the Office of the United States Trade Representative (section 1), sets its membership (section 2), functions (section 3) and administration (section 4), and provides in section 5 that it terminates after two years unless otherwise extended. I read the complete held Federal Register text, whose OCR layer prints sections 4(d), 4(e) and 5 after the page break; the dossier inventory stopped at section 4(c)(2), so I added the authority paragraph (as a clause), sections 4(d), 4(e) and 5, cut the 4(c)(2) span before the page footer, and re-entered the other clauses at their exact dossier spans (15 clauses in all). The only own-terms end is section 5: termination two years after the order unless extended. Sixteen held continuance orders (EO 12974, 13062, 13138, 13225, 13316, 13385, 13446, 13511, 13585, 13652, 13708, 13811, 13889, 14048, 14109 and 14354) each list the Committee, take effect on September 30 of an odd year and continue it for two years; I checked that each took effect no later than the date the previous one ran to, so there is no gap. EO 14354 (effective September 30, 2025) continues it until September 30, 2027 and supersedes sections 1 and 2 of EO 14109. The OFR disposition notes list the earlier continuance orders as amending EO 12905 and the later ones as continuing it, with a cross-reference to EO 13585; none revokes or supersedes it. The held text of 19 U.S.C. 2155, which the order cites for its Cabinet consultation rule, remains in the U.S. Code (held at jobs/theophilus-sources/output/texts/usc-t19-s2155.txt, which prints the order as a note, but not a packet evidence record). The three bounded searches record no revocation or supersession. All fifteen clauses are operative, checked through 2026-10-14; the section 5 clause is operative because its termination condition was displaced by extension, with the continuance chain attached as later events.
savings_reason: EO 12905 has no savings or transition clause, and no held later order revokes or replaces it; the Committee continues under EO 14354 until September 30, 2027, so no residual from an ended clause arises.
earlier_end_check: Own text: section 5 terminates the Committee two years after March 25, 1994 unless otherwise extended. That condition did not end it because sixteen held continuance orders extended it with no gap, the last until September 30, 2027. The two-year member terms in section 2(b) are appointment terms, not an end of the order. A search of the held texts for the number 12905 finds the continuance orders, Federal Register notices, the OFR notes and the U.S. Code note; none revokes or supersedes it.
scope_check: Fifteen clauses follow the order text: the authority paragraph, section 1, section 2(a) and (b), section 3(a) to (d), section 4(a), (b), (c)(1), (c)(2), (d) and (e), and section 5. Sections 4(d), 4(e) and 5 and the authority paragraph were added to the dossier inventory.
independent_command_check: Sections 1 and 5 concern the existence and term of the Committee and are continued by the held continuance orders. Sections 2, 3(a), 3(c), 3(d) and 4 are standing rules that apply while the Committee exists. Section 3(b) is a recurring report due at the conclusion of each covered negotiation, not a one-time task.
savings_check: The order has no savings, transition or accrued-rights clause, and the Committee is still continued, so no residual effect of an ended clause arises.
